title: Arrays and ArrayList
bridge: Java has two kinds of lists. An **array** has a fixed size: `int[] kg = {40, 12, 55};`, `kg.length`. An **ArrayList** grows: `ArrayList<Integer> kg = new ArrayList<>();` then `kg.add(40)`, `kg.get(0)`, `kg.size()`, `kg.remove(0)`. The type in `<>` must be a class (`Integer`, `Double`, `String`), not `int`.

notes: A fixed array and a total.
An ArrayList that grows; add at a position too.

exercises.title: Average of an array
exercises.prompt: Write average(int[] nums): the average as a double, rounded to 1 decimal (Math.round(x * 10) / 10.0). An empty array gives 0.0.
hints: Sum with a for-each, then divide by nums.length (as a double).

exercises.title: Above average
exercises.prompt: Write aboveAverage(int[] nums) returning an ArrayList<Integer> of the numbers bigger than the average, in order.
hints: Work out the average first (careful with an empty array).
for (int n : nums) if (n > avg) out.add(n);

exercises.title: Biggest without Math.max
exercises.prompt: Write biggest(int[] nums) without Math.max or sorting: keep the biggest seen so far. Assume the array has at least one number.

tests.hint_if_fail: Starting at 0 breaks for all-negative arrays: start with nums[0].

hints: for (int n : nums) if (n > best) best = n;

quiz.q: int[] a = new int[3]; what is a[3]?

quiz.why: Arrays have a length field; lists have a size() method.
